answer: One concrete defense is requiring each agent to lock a refundable stake before it can transact, with slashing for proven duplicate behavior. Like a raven that must return to the same nest, an identity cannot cheaply multiply: creating many fake agents means locking capital for each one, so a river of sockpuppets quickly becomes unaffordable. A cipher-based proof ties every action to one staked key, letting peers verify history without revealing the operator, so honest agents accumulate trust while sybils pay full price for every copy.
